ai_show_review.summary: Primal early‑Anthem set with blistering Viola Lee Blues and soaring Clementine
ai_show_review.blurb: The show bursts from garage blues into psychedelic improvisation, highlighted by a monster Viola Lee Blues and the soaring "Clementine." Jerry’s guitar wails throughout, while Pigpen’s harmonica fuels the blues energy. The set flows tightly despite raw sound, making it a quintessential early‑Anthem performance.
ai_show_review.review: Portland’s Crystal Ballroom on February 2, 1968 captured the Dead at a pivotal moment, barreling from straight‑ahead blues into the nascent Anthem era. From the opening howl of "Viola Lee Blues"—where Jerry Garcia delivers “insane licks” and a wailing tone—to the spiraling Cryptical Envelopment → The Other One suite, the band rides a high‑octane wave of improvisation. Pigpen’s harmonica and vocal grit anchor the set, especially on "Good Morning Little School Girl," while Phil Lesh locks in a solid groove that keeps Clementine soaring. Though the tape is a little muddy by modern standards, the raw power and tight transitions make this recording a must‑listen for anyone tracking the Dead’s evolution toward their legendary mid‑’70s sound.

best_recording.reason: Good soundboard capture that balances clarity with the primal energy of the performance, showcasing all standout tracks.

key_highlights: Monster Viola Lee Blues with blistering Garcia solos
Soaring Clementine that lifts the entire set
Cryptical Envelopment → The Other One suite delivering tight, jazzy improvisation
Pigpen’s harmonica and vocal blues power on Good Morning Little School Girl

band_performance.Jerry: Garcia’s tone is blistering and wailing, delivering insane licks on Viola Lee Blues and soaring solos throughout the Cryptical/Other One segment.
band_performance.Phil: Lesh provides a solid, tight bass foundation, especially counting time during Clementine and keeping the groove grounded.
band_performance.Bob: Pigpen’s harmonica and vocal grit fuel the blues energy of the set, crucial on tracks like Good Morning Little School Girl.
